newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia prices drop 6.9 pct in past nine months.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia prices drop 6.9 pct in past nine months.

text.p: Ethiopia's inflation rate fell to minus 6.9 percent in the last nine months amid vigorous economic growth, Prime Minister Meles Zenawi said on Tuesday.
GDP growth for 1997/98 was projected at between nine and 10 percent, Meles said. GDP fell 7.4 percent in 1991/92 but rose 7.7 percent in 1995, according to government figures.

"The inflationary situation has been reversed and the Ethiopian economy has been characterised by deflation," said Meles in his quarterly report to parliament quoted by the state-run Ethiopian News Agency.
"Inflation is now 6.9 percent below zero and this indicated that the purchasing power of the birr is greater by that percent than its actual value," he said.
Consumer price inflation, around 40 percent under Marxist rule, stood at minus 4.4 percent in the January-September 1996 period, according to Economist Intelligence Unit figures.
Ethiopia opted for free market reforms in 1993 and its economic policy was hailed by donors last December who pledged $2.5 billion in aid over three years.
Ethiopia has received 67 percent relief from the Paris Club on its $4.4 billion debt and could get up to 99 percent World Bank debt relief.
Economic performance during the first nine months of the 1996/97 fiscal year was "vigorous because of the strict fiscal policy that has been exercised in the country," he said.
Government revenue exceeded expenditure to a greater extent than expected and the surplus was being used to service the country's external debt.
"Over the last nine months government revenue has exceeded expenditure by 844 million birr ($127.5 million)," he said.
Ethiopia's present rulers drove former Marxist dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam from power in 1991 in an uprising that ended a 30-year civil war.
